messages:
anya: quick follow-up to the warmup RFC — thinking we should split responsibilities: a lightweight warmup-coordinator service that computes per-shard 'anchor' scores and pushes small overlay blobs (eviction hints + kv-priority) to workers, rather than having each worker run the full scoring logic. low-latency, single source of truth for prioritization.

luke: sounds promising. my main worry is the API boundary: how do workers subscribe? long-poll vs push? also failure modes if coordinator is unavailable.

michael: agree on push model + soft-state. workers should accept overlay deltas and apply them non-atomically (best-effort) so they can still operate if overlay missing. fallback: workers can run a cheap local heuristic.

sara: how does this interact with safetensors streaming vs mmap? i want to avoid creating another incompatible path. ideally overlay + streaming should work for both.

anya: good point. design idea: keep the on-disk weight format unchanged (safetensors blob shards), but define an 'overlay descriptor' that references shard byte-ranges and provides hot-priority ranges. overlay = small JSON/TLV (<= 2kb) that says: shard-id, ranges: [[off,len,score],...], compression: gzip|none, schema-v: 1. workers use ranges to prefetch via range-GET or mmap advise.

luke: can we make overlay descriptor binary/TLV so we can attach checksums and versioning cheaply? JSON is fine for prototype but we should plan for compact.

anya: agreed. sample proto we sketched:
```
POST /warmup-subscribe
{
  "model": "redwood/3b-open",
  "subscription_id": "svc-123",
  "capabilities": ["mmap","range-get","streaming-apply"]
}
```
Coordinator replies with a signed overlay descriptor and a small s3 url for the hot ranges if we need to ship blobs.

michael: operational note: overlay signing + monotonic version prevents workers applying stale overlays after a failover. also helps audits.

anya: fallback behavior: if overlay not present or version mismatch, worker falls back to: 1) local heuristic prefetch, 2) range-GET the full shard, 3) mmap the file if local path exists. we should avoid any blocking RPC on the request path — warmup is best-effort.

luke: what about atomicity when swapping quantized weight files? currently we do swap by rename which is atomic on POSIX, but if we stream partial updates overlay approach might cause inconsistent reads. need a handshake: coordinator issues 'apply-v<n>' and worker only switches pointer once all required ranges verified.

anya: exactly. propose a 2-phase: APPLY_PREPARE (download/verify ranges, write to temp fd), APPLY_COMMIT (atomic rename + update in-memory index). we already do something similar but need to formalize for streaming + gzipped chunks.

infra-bot: deploy: warmup-coordinator prototype env created on sandbox-ml (svc-warmup-pt). logs at https://internal.corp/logs/svc-warmup-pt

michael: perf question — how do we score ranges? naive token-frequency heuristic might bias transformer attention heads; alternatively use prefix-KV hotness from sampled traffic. coordinator can ingest sampled traces + model-profile to compute a score.

sara: sampling is sensitive. keep sampling opt-in and aggregated. also tag overlays with "sampled-from: production" or "synthetic-prompt".

luke: another trade: central coordinator simplifies global optimization but is single point of policy complexity. maybe allow hierarchical mode: local coordinator per rack that merges global hints with local telemetry.

anya: good call. plan: start with single warmup-coordinator + capability for local merge. next steps: write a short design doc with message formats (JSON/TLV), 2-phase apply handshake, fallback policy, and a small benchmarking harness (simulate range-get vs mmap coldstart). i'll draft the doc and tag folks.

michael: add a checklist for safety: signature verification, version monotonicity, and rollback path.

sara: please include compatibility checklist for safetensors variants (uncompressed, zstd, aligned-chunk).

anya: will do. action: i'll open a PR with the design doc and a tiny prototype service and link here. thanks all. :tada:
